nodes.name: Telegram Webhook
nodes.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-20 (live execution #847/#848/#857/#858): originally n8n-nodes-base.telegramTrigger. That node type does NOT expose raw request headers on $json -- only the already-parsed Telegram Update object (update_id, message, ...) -- so FR3's 'Verify Telegram secret' node always read an empty header and rejected every request, including legitimate ones (confirmed live: authFailed:true on a real /today message from the allowlisted chat). Switched to a generic Webhook node instead, the same convention gmail-ingestion.json / draft-generation.json / gmail-renewal-recovery.json's resync webhook already use for header-based secret verification. httpMethod=POST, responseMode='responseNode' pairs correctly with the three 'Respond 200 - ...' nodes below (a genuine webhook node is required for respondToWebhook to work at all -- also confirmed live, see those nodes' notes). No n8n credential of any kind is needed for this node; TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (used only by telegram-send.json) remains the only Telegram-related secret this change needs. The webhook must be registered manually via Telegram's setWebhook API (docs/setup/assistant-bot-setup.md step 5) pointed at this node's path -- there is no auto-registration the way telegramTrigger provided.

nodes.name: Verify Telegram secret
nodes.notes: Requires NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto and N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false on the n8n instance -- same two env vars draft-generation-setup.md documents as non-optional for its own 'Verify secret' node; without both, every request is rejected regardless of whether the secret is correct.

nodes.name: Secret ok?
nodes.notes: True (index 0, authFailed) -> Respond 200 - ack only, no reply sent (FR3, a forged call gets no signal it failed). False (index 1) -> chat-ID allowlist check.

nodes.name: Check chat allowlist
nodes.notes: FR4: fail-closed and silent -- an empty/misconfigured TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS allows nobody, never everybody.

nodes.name: Allowed?
nodes.notes: True (index 0) -> normalize the message and reach the Brain. False (index 1, unlisted chat) -> Respond 200 - ack only (FR4/AC2): no reply sent, no further action, and the sender gets no acknowledgement the bot even exists.

nodes.name: Normalize message
nodes.notes: Edge case (spec.md): non-text content (sticker/photo/voice) has isText=false -- 'Is text?' below short-circuits that to a fixed reply without ever calling the Brain.

nodes.name: Is text?
nodes.notes: True (index 0) -> Call Assistant Brain. False (index 1, sticker/photo/voice/etc.) -> Call Telegram Send with a fixed 'text only' reply, Brain never invoked.

nodes.name: Call Assistant Brain
nodes.notes: Blocking call (waitForSubWorkflow: true) per design.md's Architecture -- step 4 must complete before step 5 (Telegram Send) can run. References the 'Assistant Brain' sub-workflow by name (cachedResultName), workflowId.value left blank; re-point at the real workflow via the resource picker once assistant-brain.json is imported.

nodes.name: Call Telegram Send
nodes.notes: Blocking call, step 5. Reads chat_id from 'Normalize message' by node-name reference (Assistant Brain's own output only carries reply_text) and text from the Brain's { reply_text }. References 'Telegram Send' by name, same re-pointing step as 'Call Assistant Brain'.

nodes.name: Non-text reply

parameters.jsCode: return { json: { chat_id: $json.chat_id, reply_text: 'I can only read text right now.' } };

nodes.notes: Edge case: fixed reply for non-text messages, without invoking the Brain.

nodes.name: Call Telegram Send (non-text)
nodes.notes: Same 'Telegram Send' sub-workflow as the text path's 'Call Telegram Send' -- two separate nodes because they sit on different IF branches, not two different destinations.

nodes.name: Respond 200 - ack
nodes.notes: Terminal, all paths converge here. Telegram requires 200 to avoid retrying/disabling the webhook, regardless of whether a reply was actually sent (FR4's unlisted-chat path also reaches this node, just without ever calling the Brain or Telegram Send). RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-20: this is a respondToWebhook node again -- it was briefly changed to a NoOp under the mistaken assumption that Telegram Trigger's own auto-ack made an explicit response unnecessary, but the real fix was switching the trigger node type itself (see 'Telegram Webhook's notes) -- with a genuine Webhook node, this respondToWebhook is required and correct.

nodes.name: Respond 200 - unauthorized (silent)
nodes.notes: Terminal. FR3's signature-verification failure -- Telegram still gets 200 (a forged caller learns nothing from the response), but no chat-ID check, no Brain call, no reply. RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-20, see 'Respond 200 - ack' notes.

nodes.name: Respond 200 - unlisted chat (silent)
nodes.notes: Terminal. FR4/AC2 -- a message from a chat ID not in TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS: Telegram sees a successful delivery, the sender sees nothing. RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-20, see 'Respond 200 - ack' notes.

parameters.content:
## Telegram Adapter

Inbound: Telegram Trigger (webhook) -> verify X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token (FR3, constant-time) -> chat-ID allowlist (FR4) -> normalize to { chat_id, text, channel } -> non-text short-circuit -> blocking call to Assistant Brain -> blocking call to Telegram Send -> respond 200. Every failure path (bad secret, unlisted chat) still responds 200 to Telegram but sends no reply and reaches neither the Brain nor Telegram Send.

See .specclaw/changes/012-assistant-bot/spec.md (FR1-FR4, FR10 edge case) and design.md (Architecture).

### Placeholders to fill in on import

- **TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET** n8n environment variable -- generated per docs/setup/assistant-bot-setup.md, passed as secret_token when calling Telegram's setWebhook.
- **TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS** n8n environment variable -- comma-separated chat IDs, no spaces required (trimmed).
- 'Call Assistant Brain' and both 'Call Telegram Send' nodes reference their sub-workflows by name only (workflowId.value blank) -- re-point each at the real imported workflow via the resource picker once assistant-brain.json / telegram-send.json are imported.
- The Telegram Trigger's webhookId is a placeholder -- n8n assigns the real one on save; docs/setup/assistant-bot-setup.md then points Telegram's setWebhook at that URL.
- Requires NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto and N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false (already set for draft-generation.json/gmail-renewal-recovery.json if those are deployed -- confirm both are present, no new setting needed if so).
